liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Sugaree** (2 reviews): Reviewer names this their favorite Sugaree; Reviewer calls the Sugaree incredible, also singling out Row Jimmy and The Music Never Stopped [21][29]
- **Space** (2 reviews): Reviewer describes the space segment as having an alien quality; The Jam > Drums > Space stretch is likened to a mothership landing and then taking off again [21][22]
- **High Time** (1 review): Reviewer finds High Time full of emotion [26]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): Reviewer praises second set's Terrapin into Playin', then space into Uncle John's Band, Miracle and Bertha [29]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): Bobby nods to Pigpen during Good Lovin', quoting a line his old friend used to say about the lovelight [28]

## The recordings

- **gd1979-12-28.mtx.seamons.94267.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 156 min; rated 4.6/5 by 15 [1]
- **gd1979-12-28.140833.sbd.pcm.miller.clugston.fixed.flac1644**: soundboard; 21 songs; 160 min [3]
- **gd79-12-28.sbd.lai.4145.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 156 min; rated 4.61/5 by 56 [6]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the soundboard recording very crisp; Reviewer calls the sound of this soundboard top-notch; Reviewer hears a high-pitched whine throughout and a dulled high end, calling this copy inferior to theirs [21][23][24][25][26][28]
- **gd1979-12-28.sbd-fried.lai.19918.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 156 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [8]
- **gd1979-12-28.167366.nak700.biggar.smith.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 160 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [10]

## Around the show

- Rumor says Jerry came on stage after the show and told the tapers he definitely needed a copy [19]
- The first set has only seven songs, yet Jerry's guitar playing is outstanding throughout it [20]
- The show ended with two encores [29]
- Reviewer thinks this show, rather than 12/26, should have been the Dick's Picks release [20]
- Reviewer calls it probably the best concert of 1979 [28]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1979-12-28.mtx.seamons.94267.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [1]. Also: Chain runs soundboard to MR to PCM to DAT to WAV to FLAC; DAT supplied by Koucky and Fried; DAT played on Sony PCM-R500 through Benchmark DAC1 and Grace Lunatec, captured via LynxTwo at 24-bit/96 kHz [1]
- **gd1979-12-28.140833.sbd.pcm.miller.clugston.fixed.flac1644**: transferred by Charlie Miller and Scott Clugston; source: Master Soundboard Reels > PCM [3]. Also: A Sennheiser 421 source patches a 0:32 gap in Drums; another soundboard source supplies further small patches [3]
- **gd79-12-28.sbd.lai.4145.sbefail.shnf**: source: Soundboard [6]
- **gd1979-12-28.sbd-fried.lai.19918.shnf**: taped by Bruce Fried; transferred by Mike Lai; source: Soundboard [8]. Also: Mike Lai transferred and seeded it from Bruce Fried's DAT; sector boundary errors fixed in October 2003 [8]
- **gd1979-12-28.167366.nak700.biggar.smith.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by David Biggar; transferred by Matt Smith, Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Master 1/2 Track Audience Reels; Nakamichi 700 mics (mounted on a 30' pole) > Technics RS-1500 Reel to Reel @ 7 1/2 ips (DBX encoded) > DBX224 > 1st generation… [10]. Also: An AKG d1000e source from Mark Severson patches 1:47 in Drums [10]
